title: Nineteen Feasts and One Cracked Bowl
subtitle: 饮食与器皿 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 饮食与器皿（历史社会与文化·饮食文化与器皿）
meta: 主题语境：饮食与器皿（历史社会与文化·饮食文化与器皿）　|　核心词汇：dish　|　正文 339 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 dish 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1947 my grandmother ① cooked a dish that no neighbour in the lane would have copied, and she said the cooking was the whole of the feast. The ② dish, meaning the food and not the plate, ran nineteen feasts and stayed unpraised at the table; a dish, she said, is the only thing at a table that is judged by how long it is left untasted.

Every ③ dish in that house had the same cracked bowl under it, and the ④ dish at the end, meaning the one she kept for the guests and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever asked for twice. A dish, my aunt said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to cook; my grandmother said the patience is the part that fills nineteen feasts.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the dish was the whole of the shelf, meaning the plate and not the food. The ⑥ dish, meaning the plate and not any of that, is the only thing on a shelf that everybody counts and nobody eats; dish, he said, is either something you cook or the only word that means both a food and a plate. He said the plate is the part they remember.

By 1956 the ⑦ dish had become a line in a menu, and the menu had become an argument about the cracked bowl. The ⑧ dish of the whole thing, my grandmother wrote in November, was one house and nineteen feasts of cooking; dish, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to cook. She said the cooking was never mentioned.

The ⑨ dish I remember is the one at the end, which was served in 1970 and is still described as the strangest in the house. A ⑩ dish, my aunt said in 1972, is the only thing that improves by being shared; every dish, she said, is a plate that has agreed to look like a food. She said the plate was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 菜肴；一道菜（指桌上做出的那一份）
B. n. 菜（指那份食物本身，与那个盘子相对）
C. 固定搭配：cook a dish 烹制一道菜
D. n. 菜（指留给客人用的那一份）
E. n. 菜肴；菜品（抽象总称，指一屋子的烹调之事）
F. n. 菜（指菜单上写到、被列名的那一份）
G. n. 盘子；碟子（指架子上摆着的餐具）
H. n. 盘子（抽象总称，指人人清点却无人去吃的那些）

items.q: cooked a dish that no neighbour in the lane would have copied
The dish, meaning the food and not the plate
the dish was the whole of the shelf
the dish had become a line in a menu
The dish of the whole thing
A dish, my aunt said in 1972

answers.why: cook a dish 意为“烹制一道菜”，1947 年祖母烹制了一道巷子里没有一位邻居肯照着做的菜。
dish 意为“菜”，指那份食物本身而不是那个盘子，它历经十九次宴席而在桌上无人称赞。
dish 意为“菜肴”，指那栋房子里每一道菜，每一道下面都垫着同一只有裂纹的碗。
dish 意为“菜”，指留给客人用的那一份，是唯一有人要过两次的。
dish 意为“盘子、碟子”，指架子上摆着的餐具，叔叔说这些盘子就是那层架子的全部。
dish 意为“盘子”，指人人清点却无人去吃的那些而不是那份食物，是架子上人人都清点、却无人去吃的东西。
dish 意为“菜”，指菜单上写到、被列名的那一份，到 1956 年这道菜成了菜单里的一行。
dish 意为“菜肴、菜品”，祖母十一月写道，整件事的烹调之事是一栋房子和十九次宴席的烹饪。
dish 意为“菜”，我记得的是末尾那一份，1970 年端上桌，至今仍被说成屋里最奇的一份。
dish 为抽象总称，姑姑 1972 年说，一道菜是唯一会因为被分享而变得更好的东西。
